Subject: Project Meridian: APAC microregion pilot & tri-region capacity ask

Team —

Following the demo with NovaCorp yesterday, they asked for a tight pilot in Singapore plus a lightweight US/EU fallback for low-latency routing. They want a predictable committed lane for their initial production window (Q1 next year) and the ability to burst additional nodes for peak workloads. High-level asks: 

- Pilot start: mid-November 2026 (2 month pilot)
- Pilot footprint: Singapore microregion (edge) — target 18 sustained concurrent generation slots for G4-like workloads; 4 immediate burst nodes for nightly batch runs
- Fallback lanes: small US and EU pools (6 slots each) with auto-failover for regional outages
- Model profile: 70/30 mix gen/chat vs embeddings; typical sequence length 512 tokens; KV caching expected

Attached is my initial sizing sheet (Meridian_Sizing_Sheet_v2.xlsx). Can you: 
1) Ben — confirm approximate node counts and whether we can meet the 18 sustained slot target on APAC hardware mix without impacting other pilots. Include quantization options and likely token cost delta.
2) Karthik — assuming this gets committed as a 12-month reserved pool, what tranche/commit levels do we need to propose to procurement (pricing buckets)? Also include expected lead times for Singapore procurement.
3) Marissa — does this mapping look feasible for a Dedicated pilot SOW (timeline and gating items)?

I'll loop in the NovaCorp POC after we have a clearer number.

Thanks — Mina

--
Mina Haddad

Subject: Re: Project Meridian: APAC microregion pilot & tri-region capacity ask

Mina —

Quick read of the sizing sheet. Initial thoughts:

- 18 sustained slots in SG is reasonable if we use 80% packed A100S-equivalent instances with int8 quantization for the 70% gen/chat workload. That gets latency under 150ms p50 for 512 tokens if we dedicate 2 shards per instance for KV cache locality.
- For the 4 nightly batch nodes, we can schedule them as preemptible burst capacity in the same region to avoid long-term reservation cost.
- US/EU fallbacks at 6 slots each should be single-zone small pools (T4s or equivalent) with a routable policy — good for SLA graceful degradation but not for sustained heavy throughput.
- Risk: supplier lead time for SG specialized hardware can be 8–12 weeks if we require specific NVLink configs. If they accept slightly lower performance (longer tail latency), we can cut to 4–6 weeks using standard instances.

I'll put hard numbers in the attached sheet and estimate ops effort to isolate pilot capacity.

Ben

Pricing and procurement notes:

- Suggested SKU mix for the committed tranche: 12 medium nodes (sustained) in SG, 4 burst-capable nodes (reservation optional), US/EU each 6 small nodes on a month-to-month standing reservation.
- Expected price bands (ballpark): committed medium node $X, burst node 30% premium when on-demand; full quote in sheet.
- Procurement gating: SOC2 attestation (NovaCorp asked) and a simple IP/data residency clause for EU. That will influence whether EU fallback requires additional controls (likely yes).
- Lead time estimate: 6 weeks if they accept standard instance SKUs; 10+ weeks for NVLink/heterogeneous racks.

I'll draft a tranche proposal and proposed billing cadence for the HubSpot deal record (DEAL-7834).

Thanks team — appreciate the quick turnaround. A few clarifications from our side before we sign the pilot SOW: 

- Can the Singapore microregion guarantee physical separation for the pilot (separate tenant/VPC)? We need assurance for our audit team.
- For the fallback lanes, we need EU to be within an EU jurisdiction (data-at-rest restriction). If we do an EU fallback, we will require a GDPR-compliant routing policy and an addendum in the SOW.
- Lead time is a concern — 6 weeks is acceptable but we need a firm go/no-go by Oct 1 to meet our launch target.
- Please include an explicit capacity uplift option in the pilot (ability to add +8 sustained slots on 7 days' notice). That will let us absorb traffic spikes during trials.

Looking forward to the 1-page SOW and the pricing tranche.

Sanjeev
Head of ML Infrastructure, NovaCorp
